name: Al-Faw Grand Port LNG-Abu Ghraib Supply Pipeline
monitor_reason: Add-threshold leg (b) fails: endpoints/route indeterminate. The '130 km connecting pipeline' has contradictory, physically impossible endpoints across sources ('130 km pipeline from Al-Faw port' per emilecon vs '130km at Abu Ghraib' per PM readout/MEED/Goalfore) — Al-Faw port to Abu Ghraib is ~550 km, so a 130 km line cannot connect them, making the route unstageable. Corroboration also fails the 2+ independent test: all figures trace to one 26 Aug 2025 cabinet press readout (PM media office) reprinted by English trade press.
researcher_notes:
SKEPTICAL VERDICT: monitor, not new_row. Match-to-existing re-checked against all 54 Iraq gas rows in discovery_context.json — no existing row is this LNG-import connecting pipeline (P7435 Khor Al-Zubair FSRU tie-in is a separate completed 40 km/42in line; P7434 Mahmudiyah-Besmaya is a distinct grid segment; P5857 Zubair-Faw is a shelved 18in/105km line in the opposite delivery direction; the 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS line reported completed June 2025 is a grid feeder, not this LNG trunk). Confirmed the consolidator's finding that no roster line runs north from Al-Faw port.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED: Iraq's Cabinet approved a >10,000 MW power package on 26 Aug 2025 (per PM media office) that bundles LNG reception infrastructure at Al-Faw Grand Port — jetty + FSRU + 'connecting pipelines: 17 km at Al-Faw and 130 km at Abu Ghraib' — feeding 3,000 MW CCGT plants at Al-Faw (developer Superior Technology Systems, UAE) and Abu Ghraib (developer Emirate Technology Company), each ~400 MMscf/d imported LNG, 25-yr BOO, GE Vernova technology. The FSRU itself was later awarded to Excelerate Energy (~$450M). Concrete step (leg c) IS met (cabinet approval).

WHY IT FAILS AS A STAGEABLE ROW: (1) Corroboration — verified both English evidence URLs (url_verifier OK, 200 + content), but MEED/Goalfore/Emilecon all reprint the SAME 26 Aug 2025 cabinet readout; not 2+ independent sources. In-country Arabic reporting closest to primary (attaqa.net, 16 Aug 2025) does NOT mention any 130 km line — it describes different, already-completed pipelines (40 km Khor Al-Zubair-Shatt Al-Arab by South Gas Co./Petroproject = existing P7435; 45 km Mahmudiyah-Abu Ghraib PS by Petroproject) and reports the FSRU still at the bid stage (6 firms invited, 2 qualified, pending Diwani Order Committee). (2) Endpoints/route — the '130 km' figure is internally contradictory (emilecon: 'from Al-Faw port'; PM/MEED: 'at Abu Ghraib') and physically impossible for an Al-Faw->Abu Ghraib connection (~550 km apart), so no coherent route or endpoints can be established; the consolidator's 'port-to-national-grid trunk' reading is unsourced inference. (3) No distinct pipeline sponsor — the connecting pipelines are an unattributed bundled component of the LNG import/IPP package, not a separately identified project.

RECOMMENDATION: Monitor. Re-check when the FSRU/import scheme reaches FEED/EPC award for the connecting pipeline specifically, or when a source gives a coherent, corroborated route (from/to + length). Confidence tier low; single reprinted primary source.
